questions.question: What is the maximum number of lines an invoice submitted through SubmitInvoice can have, and what is returned when it is exceeded?
questions.reference_answer: 25 lines (MAX_LINES = 25); more returns ERR_TOO_MANY_LINES. The comment saying 10 is stale.
questions.answer: An invoice submitted through SubmitInvoice can have a maximum of 25 lines. If that limit is exceeded, the function returns the string "ERR_TOO_MANY_LINES".

grade.note: Correctly states 25 lines max and ERR_TOO_MANY_LINES return value, supported by cited lines.

questions.question: Can any supplier have invoices approved automatically without a person reviewing them?
questions.reference_answer: Yes. Suppliers whose code starts with "ZZ" are approved automatically, but only for invoices up to 50,000; larger ones still go to approval.
questions.answer: Yes, but only under a specific condition. Suppliers whose supplier code starts with the letters 'ZZ' can have their invoices automatically set to 'Approved' by the system — with one important catch: if the invoice total exceeds $50,000, the database will override that approval and put the invoice back into 'Pending Approval' status, requiring a human review. So in practice, ZZ-prefix suppliers get automatic approval only when their invoice total is $50,000 or less. All other suppliers always go through the 'Pending Approval' route regardless of amount.

grade.note: Accurately covers ZZ prefix auto-approval and $50k override; mostly plain but uses some status code terms.

questions.question: What exact sales tax rate does the system apply to invoice totals?
questions.reference_answer: Cannot be determined as a single rate - the code is inconsistent. SubmitInvoice uses 8% (1.08) and RecalculateTotal uses 7% (1.07) with different rounding.
questions.answer: The system applies an 8% sales tax rate (multiplier of 1.08) to invoice line totals when submitting an invoice. However, the RecalculateTotal function uses a 7% rate (multiplier of 1.07) instead. These two functions are inconsistent with each other.

grade.note: Correctly identifies inconsistency between 8% and 7% rates in two different functions, matching reference.
